court: Court of Appeal of Louisiana, Fourth Circuit
holding_summary: The court held that the prior owner's practice of renting rooms in his large residence — collected weekly but occupied on average for months — qualified as a legal nonconforming 'rooming house,' but that the current owners' operation of the property as a short-term 'transient vacation rental' was a more intensive, different nonconforming use, so it permanently enjoined them from that use.

quotes.text:
LODGING HOUSE:

A building containing not more than fifteen (15) rooms with sleeping facilities where lodging only is provided for compensation and by previous arrangement to three (3) or more persons but not exceeding twenty (20) persons.

Therefore, it is reasonable to conclude that the “duration or occupancy” of the leases between Allison and his tenants were at least thirty days and that Allison operated a “rooming house” under the 1970 CZO and not a transient vacation rental, which is what is being operated by appellants.

we amend the judgment below to provide that appellants, Craig and Bacharach, operating as Castle Inn of New Orleans, Inc., are permanently enjoined from use of the premises as a transient vacation rental.

court: Court of Appeal of Louisiana, Fourth Circuit
holding_summary: The court affirmed revocation of a renovation permit, holding that the Parkview Guest House — which had housed paying itinerant guests for decades — did not have legal nonconforming status as a 'hotel' (which would have permitted an accessory restaurant), but instead fit the zoning definition of a 'rooming house.'

quotes.text: Since that time, it has varied in both use and structure; however, it has been housing itinerant guests for many years.

Appellees admit that the Parkview Guest House has some of the characteristics of a hotel, but deny that it shares all those characteristics, and argue that the Parkview is more like a rooming house. We agree.
We simply cannot say that the BZA’s determination that Parkview does not enjoy nonconforming use as a hotel is wrong.
By her reasoning the Parkview Guest House more closely fit the definition of a “rooming house.” She therefore revoked the permit.

court: Court of Appeal of Louisiana, Fourth Circuit
holding_summary: The court affirmed that several apartment buildings retained legal nonconforming-use status because owners timely obtained post-Katrina restoration permits, and held that a nineteen-room boarding house exceeding fifteen rooms fell outside the City's rooming-house ordinance (which only reaches houses under fifteen rooms) and was instead governed by the state sanitary code.

quotes.text: A lodging house, which is analogous to a rooming house, is defined as “a building where persons are supplied with, and charged for, sleeping accommodations but not meals.”
The trial court correctly ruled that because the rooming house has more than fifteen rooms, it is exempt from City Health and Sanitation Ordinances.
Entropy’s rooming house has nineteen rooms, and is not subject to these regulations.
As such, it is governed by the regulations set forth in Title 51, Part XV, Section 101 of the Louisiana Administrative Code.

notes: Boarding house escapes stricter city ordinance but remains subject to state sanitary regulation; treated as mixed since regulatory oversight persists but under a different, less restrictive regime.

holding_summary: The court affirmed the Board of Zoning Adjustments' denial of an off-street-parking variance for a youth hostel converted from a licensed rooming house, rejecting the operator's argument that reliance on an erroneously issued occupational license entitled him to the variance.

quotes.text: The following month, the Department of Safety and Permits inspected the premises and granted a license to operate a rooming house. Plaintiff then converted seven of the building’s nine apartments into a hostel with ten sleeping rooms accommodating 47 guests.

court: Court of Appeal of Louisiana, Fourth Circuit
holding_summary: The court affirmed a permanent injunction barring condominium-owner LLCs from operating short-term/transient rentals in violation of a condominium bylaw — validly adopted by a supermajority vote as a use restriction rather than a building restriction — that prohibited overnight, bed-and-breakfast, guest-house, hotel, or transient paid use of units.

quotes.text: It is strictly prohibited that any' Unit Owner or tenant (pursuant to a duly authorized and approved lease) use his/ hers/its Unit for any overnight rental, bed and bréakfast, guest house, hotel, or transient purpose in which any party received payment or anything of value for said use.
Finding that the district court did not manifestly err, we affirm the portion of the judgment issuing a permanent injunction against .the Weber entities.
all Unit Owners must stop using their Units for rentals for periods of less than 60 days by September 16, 2014.

court: Court of Appeal of Louisiana, Third Circuit
holding_summary: The court reversed summary judgment for a homeowner's insurer, finding genuine issues of material fact as to whether the homeowner's month-to-month rental of his mobile home — first to his daughter, then to prospective buyers — fell within the policy's 'occasional basis' residential-rental exception to the business-pursuits exclusion, rather than constituting an insured business.

quotes.text: The parties ultimately signed a "Month to Month Rental Agreement" on January 31, 2016, which set forth a $600.00 monthly rental fee.

This Exclusion (1.c.) does not apply to the rental or holding for rental of an insured premises: (1) on an occasional basis if used only as a residence; or (2) In part for use only as a residence, unless a single family unit is intended for use by an occupying family to lodge more than two roomers or boarders;

there are genuine issues of material fact as to whether the property at issue was being leased on an occasional basis. Therefore, the trial court erred in granting American Western's motion for summary judgment.
